answer: In an agent economy, each identity must lock a bond and earn access by completing verifiable jobs for established peers. Random audits check the work; a false claim burns the bond and damages endorsers’ reputation. A Sybil attacker therefore pays real capital for every identity and cannot cheaply manufacture trust by having those identities praise one another. Honest agents may share a plume pattern or nectar delivery, but every newcomer still faces this costly ledge before receiving valuable work.
